correctness.rationale: A set is vertex-edge dominating exactly when its closed-neighborhood union is a vertex cover. All two-set types are eliminated: same-side and deleted matching pairs fail totality, while an adjacent cross-pair leaves a joined pair outside its closed neighborhood. The claimed three-sets are total and leave at most one vertex outside the closed-neighborhood union. Conversely, any total three-set has a two-plus-one bipartition profile, and totality forces the singleton-side index to differ from both same-side indices. The symbolic proof therefore gives the exact value, classification, and count; exhaustive finite checks match it.

value.rationale: Crown graphs are the canonical perfect-matching deletion of balanced complete bipartite graphs. The theorem identifies a sharp one-unit perturbation of total vertex-edge domination and completely describes how the missing matching forces three distinct indices in every optimum. The exact optimizer count \(n(n-1)(n-2)\) is natural structural information beyond the scalar parameter.
